To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the tongue is densely innervated with mechanoreceptors that include Piezo2+ endings of Krause end bulbs and taste bud-associated neurons, whereas the palate and gums are innervated by Merkel cells, Meissner corpuscles and glia-associated glomeruli.
the oral mucosa is innervated by a diverse array of sensory endings, which are organized in distinct topological arrangements.

(i) we identified a novel class of mechanosensory endings innervating the tongue epithelium, (ii) we found that the palate is equipped with a diverse array of mechanosensories, (iii) we found that Merkel cell numbers in the palate are age-dependent and decline at key time points in aging, and (iv) we identified a population of Merkel cells in the tongue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sensory architecture of the oral cavity and how this changes during normal aging.
the molecular and structural basis of oral mechanoreception and its age-related decline.
the molecular and cellular biology of mechanosensation, and its application to the study of sensory disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the oral cavity is equipped with a complex array of sensory afferent endings that are involved in the detection of mechanical stimuli, and the loss of these mechanoreceptors is a likely contributing factor to age-related oral dysfunction.
the oral cavity of mice is densely innervated by a variety of anatomical and molecularly distinct mechanoreceptors that exhibit a complex and organized pattern of distribution.

the tongue, palate and gums are equipped with a diverse array of mechanosensory endings that are organized in a precise and complex fashion to provide a highly specialized and sensitive system for oral tactile perception.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

oral mechanoreception is a complex and dynamic process that is orchestrated by the spatial arrangement of mechanosensitive endings and the mechanical properties of epithelial structures, such as filiform papillar ridges and taste papillae.
the oral cavity is equipped with a complex array of sensory afferent endings that are distributed in an organized fashion and may contribute to mechanosensation during oral functions.
the oral epithelia are equipped with a rich array of sensory endings that can detect a wide variety of mechanical stimuli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tongue and palate are equipped with a diverse array of putative tactile receptors that are organized in a precise and topologically defined manner.
the oral cavity is equipped with an intricate array of putative sensory receptors, including Merkel cells, Meissner corpuscles and glomus-like endings.

the oral mucosa is endowed with a rich and diverse array of putative sensory receptors that are distributed according to the topology of the epithelium and that these receptors are subject to age-dependent remodeling.
